result.title: Reinforcement Learning for Inventory Control under Regime-Switching Demand: A Controlled Comparison of LSTM, MLP, and (s,S) Policies
result.summary: Classical inventory policies such as (s,S) are provably optimal under stationary demand but cannot adapt when demand switches between hidden regimes, and memoryless deep reinforcement learning policies, confined to a fixed observation window, cannot maintain a belief over latent demand structure. We ask whether a recurrent policy offers a measurable advantage over both a memoryless policy and a classical baseline under regime-switching demand, and how that advantage scales with supply-chain lead time. We build a custom Gymnasium environment in which daily demand is generated by a two-state hidden Markov process with Poisson emissions, so that the regime is known at evaluation time but hidden from the agent. An optimised (s,S) heuristic, an MLP PPO agent, and an LSTM Recurrent PPO agent are trained under matched compute and evaluated at lead times of 0, 3, 6, and 10 days over 30 deterministic episodes each. The recurrent policy outperforms both alternatives at every lead time, and its margin over the MLP widens monotonically with lead time, from parity at lead time 0 to 2.17$\times$ at lead time 10. Principal component analysis of the LSTM hidden state explains the widening gap: the representation shifts from encoding a binary regime indicator at short lead times to encoding multi-step pipeline state at long lead times. Recurrent memory becomes the decisive architectural factor as the credit-assignment horizon lengthens.

AI.brief_summary: 在需求在隐藏两状态间切换的库存控制环境中，以匹配算力比较 (s,S) 启发式、MLP PPO 与 LSTM PPO 在 0–10 天提前期下的表现，并用隐藏状态 PCA 解释循环策略优势随提前期扩大的来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉推理，但「循环状态需维持对隐藏变量的信念、且优势随信用分配跨度增长」以及用 PCA 探测隐藏状态编码内容，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否承载任务必要信息及长视野收益的来源。
